//! Operator preflight runs the real activation on a private disk-backed snapshot.
// REL3 owns dormant-visibility counts here; SURF clause narration lives in release_narration.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#92-exact-preview-and-operator-vocabulary — no live pointer, generation or audit changes.
use super::*;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
struct Snapshot(PathBuf);
impl Drop for Snapshot {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
    }
}

pub(super) fn preview(
    store_path: &Path,
    root: PathBuf,
    release: u64,
    options: &Options,
    held_owner: Option<&crate::store_owner::Owner>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let bound = super::releases::bound_at(root.clone())?;
    let project = Project { root };
    let native = crate::native::prepare(&project, &bound).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    crate::dev_worker::prepare_release(&project,&bound.schema)?;
    let id = snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default())
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let snapshot = Snapshot(std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("snapback4-release-preview-{id}")));
    snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(&snapshot.0).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let path = snapshot.0.join("store.sqlite");
    // Probe the existing filesystem lock, independently of any HTTP address
    // hint. Keep a stopped store excluded through preview; never create a lock
    // sidecar or mutate its address record just to inspect ownership.
    let (live,_stopped_guard)=if held_owner.is_some() {(false,None)} else if store_path.exists() {
        let database=store_path.canonicalize().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
        match snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(&database,&snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&database),false,0) {
            Ok(owner)=>match owner.try_lock() {
                Ok(())=>(false,Some(owner)),
                Err(std::fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock)=>(true,None),
                Err(std::fs::TryLockError::Error(e))=>return Err(format!("preview owner probe failed: {e}")),
            },
            Err(e) if e.kind()==std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound=>(false,None),
            Err(e)=>return Err(format!("preview owner probe failed: {e}")),
        }
    }else{(false,None)};
    // SQLite VACUUM INTO takes a coherent read snapshot even with a live WAL writer.
    // Busy/disk errors refuse this preview; never fall back to copying database bytes.
    if store_path.exists() {
    let source = snapback4_core::Store::open_read_only(store_path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    source
        .conn()
        .execute("VACUUM INTO ?1", [path.to_string_lossy().as_ref()])
        .map_err(|e| {
            format!("snapshot preview failed (retry after store/disk becomes available): {e}")
        })?;
    drop(source);
    }
    let mut store = snapback4_core::Store::open(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let held = store
        .release_status(0, None, None)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#4-staging-clock — preview uses the owning host's authoritative time, without minting or advancing anything.
    let activation_now=if live {
        let status=crate::release_control::request(store_path.parent().ok_or("preview store has no deployment directory")?,crate::release_control::Command::Status{after:0,items_after:None,event:None})?;
        if status["revision"]!=held["revision"] {return Err("preview raced release activation; retry against the current store".into());}
        status["clock"]["now"].as_i64().ok_or("serving owner does not expose its activation clock; restart it with this CLI before preview")?
    }else{snapback4_core::now_ms()};
    let mut activation =
        snapback4_core::engine::release::ReleaseActivation::new(release, held["release"].as_u64());
    activation.expected_revision = held["revision"].as_u64();
    activation.native_digest = native.installed.map(|n| n.digest);
    activation.operation = "preview".into();
    activation.restore_dormant = !options.flags.contains_key("deploy-direction") || options.flags.contains_key("restore-dormant");
    let mut steps = Vec::new();
    let estimate = store
        .adoption_estimate(&bound.schema)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
        .map(|e| e.summary());
    let candidate_schema=bound.schema.clone();
    let candidate_programs:std::collections::BTreeMap<_,_>=bound.programs.iter().map(|p|(p.program.name.clone(),p.program.clone())).collect();
    let mut hazards=Vec::new();
    let mut notes=Vec::new();
    let prior:Option<(String,String)>=store.conn().query_row("SELECT schema,programs FROM _generations WHERE generation=(SELECT CAST(value AS INTEGER) FROM _meta WHERE key='generation')",[],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?))).ok();
    let prior_schema=prior.as_ref().map(|(schema,_)|serde_json::from_str::<snapback4_core::Schema>(schema).map_err(|e|e.to_string())).transpose()?;
    if let Some((schema,programs))=prior {
        let prior:snapback4_core::Schema=serde_json::from_str(&schema).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
        steps=snapback4_core::successor::classify(&prior,&candidate_schema);
        let programs:std::collections::BTreeMap<String,snapback4_core::ir::Program>=serde_json::from_str(&programs).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
        let target_label = format!("release {release}");
        let compatibility = super::release_narration::compatibility(&store, &prior, &candidate_schema, held["release"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0), &target_label, options.flags.contains_key("deploy-direction"))?;
        for line in compatibility {
            if let Some(warning) = line.strip_prefix("WARNING ") { hazards.push(warning.to_owned()); }
            else { notes.push(line.trim_start_matches("note: ").to_owned()); }
        }
        let rollback=!options.flags.contains_key("deploy-direction");
        let (behavior_warnings, behavior_notes) = super::release_narration::behavior(store_path, &store, &prior, &candidate_schema, &programs, &candidate_programs, &project, held["release"].as_u64(), &target_label, rollback)?;
        hazards.extend(behavior_warnings); notes.extend(behavior_notes);
        for name in prior.tables.keys().filter(|name|!candidate_schema.tables.contains_key(*name) && prior.maintain_for(name).is_none() && prior.tables[*name].ephemeral.is_none()) {
            let count:u64=store.conn().query_row("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM r WHERE t=(SELECT num FROM _catalog WHERE name=?1)",[name],|r|r.get::<_,i64>(0).map(|n|n as u64)).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if count>0 {hazards.push(format!("table {name}: {count} rows become dormant; {target_label} lacks this table's behavior; preserve it in a bridge or accept its absence"));}
        }
    }
    super::release_safeguards::capture(&store)?;
    let mut engine = snapback4_core::Engine::new_release_prepared_at(
        store,
        bound.schema,
        bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program),
        &activation,
        options.flags.contains_key("allow-feed-adoption"),
        activation_now,
    )
    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut planned = engine
        .store_mut()
        .release_status(0, None, None)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    planned["items"] = serde_json::to_value(
        engine
            .store_mut()
            .dormant_inventory(None, usize::MAX)
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
    )
    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let items: Vec<snapback4_core::store::DormantItem> = serde_json::from_value(planned["items"].clone()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut effects = super::release_safeguards::warnings(engine.store(),prior_schema.as_ref(),&candidate_schema,&candidate_programs,&items,release,!options.flags.contains_key("deploy-direction"))?;
    effects.append(&mut hazards); hazards=effects;
    for fill in &engine.store().adoption_report.backfills { notes.push(format!("backfill: {fill}; confirm these historical values before selecting release {release}")); }
    steps.retain(|step|!step.message.contains("engine capture"));
    for step in &mut steps {
        if step.change==snapback4_core::successor::Change::Narrowing {
            step.change=snapback4_core::successor::Change::Additive;
            step.message=format!("{}; active rows satisfy the candidate after dormant projection",step.message.split(';').next().unwrap_or(&step.message));
        }
        if let Some(position)=step.path.strip_prefix("maintains[").and_then(|s|s.strip_suffix(']')).and_then(|s|s.parse::<usize>().ok()) {
            let label=candidate_schema.maintains[position].label();
            let visits=engine.store().adoption_report.views.iter().find(|view|view.name==label).map(|v|v.rows).unwrap_or(0);
            step.message=format!("maintain {label}: rebuilt from {visits} source rows");
            step.change=snapback4_core::successor::Change::Additive;
        }
        let path=step.path.strip_prefix("tables.").unwrap_or(&step.path).replace(".columns.",".");
        let count=planned["items"].as_array().into_iter().flatten().find(|i|i["path"].as_str()==Some(path.as_str())).and_then(|i|i["rows"].as_u64()).unwrap_or(0);
        let unit = if step.path.contains(".columns.") { "cells" } else if step.path.contains(".indexes.") { "entries" } else { "rows" };
        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#11-wave-11-factual-release-narration — per-path prose uses the same disjoint counts as the inventory totals.
        let retained = if count == 0 && unit == "cells" {
            format!("no standalone {unit} become dormant (cells of any dormant rows are counted with those rows)")
        } else if count == 0 {
            format!("no {unit} become dormant")
        } else {
            format!("its {unit} become dormant ({count} {unit}; restored on forward)")
        };
        step.message=step.message.replace("its rows are lost", &retained).replace("its values are lost", &retained);
    }
    let checklist = super::release_bridge::checklist(held["release"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),release,&hazards);
    if let Some(path) = options.flags.get("bridge") {
        let current = held["release"].as_u64().ok_or("a bridge needs a current deployed release")?;
        super::release_bridge::write(Path::new(path),store_path.parent().ok_or("no deployment directory")?,current,release,&checklist)?;
        eprintln!("bridge starter written to {path}; edit its current source and follow ROLLBACK-CHECKLIST.md before activation");
    }
    if options.json {
        println!("{}",serde_json::to_string_pretty(&serde_json::json!({"preview":true,"checklist":checklist,"hazards":hazards,"notes":notes,"current":held,"plan":planned,"steps":steps,"estimate":estimate,"phases":engine.store().adoption_report.summary(),"backfills":engine.store().adoption_report.backfills})).unwrap());
    } else {
        println!("preview: release {release} would be current as generation {}; live release unchanged", engine.generation());
        super::release_summary::print(prior_schema.as_ref(), &candidate_schema, &candidate_programs, &hazards, &notes, &steps, &items);
        if !options.flags.contains_key("deploy-direction") { println!("  checklist: prove the named refusal cases and affected lists/counts as real accounts before release {release}; `--bridge <new-dir>` saves current source plus this app's ROLLBACK-CHECKLIST.md"); }
        println!("  storage: {}",snapback4_core::store::adoption_report::AdoptionReport::dormant(&items));
        if options.flags.contains_key("verbose") {
            for hazard in hazards { println!("  detail: WARNING {hazard}"); }
            for note in notes { println!("  detail: note: {note}"); }
            for step in steps {println!("  {}: {}",step.path,step.message);}
            for item in &items { println!("  {}: {} {} dormant (restored on compatible forward); sample ids [{}]", item.key, item.rows, item.unit(), item.sample_ids.join(", ")); }
            println!("{}", engine.store().adoption_report.summary());
            if let Some(estimate) = estimate {
                println!("{estimate}");
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
//! Owner-mediated release publication in the running HTTP process.
use super::*;
use crate::release_control::Command;
#[cfg(unix)]
use crate::release_control::Listener;
use snapback4_core::engine::release::ReleaseActivation;

#[cfg(unix)]
pub(super) fn start(
    shared: Arc<Shared>,
    dir: std::path::PathBuf,
) -> Result<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>, String> {
    let store = shared
        .owner
        .as_ref()
        .ok_or("release control requires a persisted owner")?
        .path()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let listener = Listener::bind(&dir, store)?;
    crate::lifecycle::managed_cleanup();
    crate::lifecycle::background("release-control", move || {
        listener.run(|command| apply(&shared, &dir, command))
    })
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5-hot-activation-and-ownership — only assignments and committed rebind follow the database commit.
pub(super) fn apply(
    shared: &Shared,
    dir: &std::path::Path,
    command: Command,
) -> Result<Json, String> {
    match command {
        Command::Status {
            after,
            items_after,
            event,
        } => {
            let mut engine=lock(&shared.engine);
            let mut status=engine.store_mut().release_status(after,items_after.as_deref(),event).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            status["clock"]=json!({"now":shared.now(),"offsetMs":lock(&shared.clock).offset()});
            Ok(status)
        },
        Command::Prune {
            confirm,
            expected_revision,
        } => {
            let mut result = lock(&shared.engine)
                .store_mut()
                .prune_dormant(confirm, Some(expected_revision))
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if let Some(items) = result["items"].as_array_mut() {
                items.truncate(16);
            }
            result["items_after"] = result["items"]
                .as_array()
                .and_then(|items| items.last())
                .map(|i| i["key"].clone())
                .unwrap_or(Json::Null);
            Ok(result)
        }
        Command::Activate {
            release,
            expected_release,
            expected_revision,
            digest,
            rollback,
            restore_dormant,
            allow_feed_adoption,
        } => {
            if release == 0 {
                return Err("release id must be positive".into());
            }
            let project = Project {
                root: dir.join("releases").join(release.to_string()),
            };
            if !std::fs::symlink_metadata(&project.root)
                .is_ok_and(|m| m.is_dir() && !m.file_type().is_symlink())
            {
                return Err(format!(
                    "release {release} is not an immutable release directory"
                ));
            }
            if crate::release_files::digest(&project.root)? != digest {
                return Err("staged release content changed; redeploy its exact source".into());
            }
            if project.sources().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_empty() {
                return Err(format!(
                    "release {release} has no Quarry source; select a complete immutable release"
                ));
            }
            let bound = project.compile().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
                return Err(bound
                    .diagnostics
                    .iter()
                    .map(ToString::to_string)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    .join("\n"));
            }
            let prepared = crate::native::prepare(&project, &bound).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            crate::dev_worker::prepare_release(&project, &bound.schema)?;
            crate::release_files::link_store(&project.root)?;
            if crate::release_files::digest(&project.root)? != digest {
                return Err("release artifacts changed during preparation; retry after inspecting immutable source".into());
            }
            crate::release_files::durable(&project.root)?;
            let mut pointer =
                crate::release_files::Pointer::prepare(dir, release, expected_release, rollback)?;
            let options = ReleaseActivation {
                release,
                expected_previous: expected_release,
                expected_revision: Some(expected_revision),
                restore_dormant,
                native_digest: prepared.installed.as_ref().map(|m| m.digest.clone()),
                operation: if rollback { "rollback" } else { "deploy" }.into(),
            };
            let _requests=shared.release_requests.write();
            let mut engine = lock(&shared.engine);
            lock(&shared.readers).begin_adoption(&bound);
            let generation = match engine.adopt_release_at(
                bound.schema.clone(),
                bound.programs.iter().map(|p| p.program.clone()),
                &options,
                allow_feed_adoption,
                shared.now(),
            ) {
                Ok(generation) => generation,
                Err(error) => {
                    lock(&shared.readers).finish_adoption();
                    return Err(error.to_string());
                }
            };
            #[cfg(test)]
            test_work(&shared.release_committed);
            engine.set_prepared_native(prepared.module);
            engine.set_presence(Some(shared.presence.clone()));
            shared.refresh_time_audience_clock(&engine, shared.now());
            lock(&shared.readers).replace(&engine, &bound.refusal_sites);
            {
                let mut active = lock(&shared.bound);
                let mut advertised = lock(&shared.generation);
                let mut native = lock(&shared.native);
                shared.latency.adopt(&bound);
                *active = bound;
                *advertised = generation;
                *native = prepared.installed;
                let mut root = lock(&shared.release_root);
                *root = Some(project.root);
                shared.worker_revision.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Release);
            }
            crate::lifecycle::generation(generation);
            shared.publish_engine(&engine);
            // Completion I/O can fail, but never abandons the new runtime.
            pointer.finish(generation)?;
            snapback4_core::diagnostic!(
                "snapback4 serve: release {release} activated without restart as generation {generation}"
            );
            Ok(
                json!({"release":release,"generation":generation,"revision":expected_revision+1,"hot":true,"adoption":engine.store().adoption_report.compact(),"details":engine.store().adoption_report.summary(),"backfills":engine.store().adoption_report.backfills}),
            )
        }
    }
}

 seed(&mut e,"bookings",json!({"id":"c","owner":"user:x"}));let g=e.generation();
 let error=adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap_err().to_string();assert!(error.contains("historical lookup")&&error.contains("not unique")&&error.contains("2 affected rows"),"{error}");assert_eq!(g,e.generation());
}

#[test]
fn removal_of_last_opening_boundary_keeps_the_durable_retirement_floor() {
 let old="table items:\n  opens: time\n  until: time\n  n: int\n  not before .opens\n  expire at .until\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let next=old.replace("  not before .opens\n","").replace("  expire at .until\n","")+"backfill items prolong(until: time):\n  {until:until + 1d}\n";
 for requested in [1,100] {
  let(s,p)=compile(old);let mut e=Engine::new_release_prepared_at(Store::memory().unwrap(),s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(1,None),false,0).unwrap();
  let r=wire::row_from_json(&e.schema().tables["items"],&json!({"id":"a","opens":0,"until":50,"n":3})).unwrap();e.seed_at([("items".into(),r)],0).unwrap();
  {let tx=e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();tx.pin_time_audience_clock(100).unwrap();tx.commit().unwrap();}
  let(s,p)=compile(&next);e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(2,Some(1)),false,requested).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(e.store().count("items").unwrap(),0,"source deadline before persisted floor, requested={requested}");
 }
}

#[test]
fn reentry_restores_shared_snapshots_for_arguments_and_point_reads() {
 let old="table items:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let twice=old.to_owned()+"backfill items twice(n: int):\n  {n:n * 2}\n";
 for later in [false,true] {
  let copied=twice.replace("  n: int","  copied: int\n  lookedUp: int\n  n: int")+"backfill items copy(n: int, id: items):\n  {copied:n, lookedUp:(items[id] ! else NOT_FOUND).n}\n";
  let mut e=engine(old);seed(&mut e,"items",json!({"id":"a","n":3}));
  if later {adopt(&mut e,&twice,2).unwrap();}
  adopt(&mut e,&copied,3).unwrap();let expected=if later {6}else{3};
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","copied"),Value::Int(expected));
  adopt(&mut e,"query empty():\n  return true\n",4).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&copied,3).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","n"),Value::Int(6));assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","copied"),Value::Int(expected));assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","lookedUp"),Value::Int(expected));
 }
}

#[test]
fn partial_table_reentry_restores_carried_declarations_in_the_same_cohort() {

 let parent_fill="backfill parents twice(n: int):\n  {n:n * 2}\n";

 let mut e=engine(&old);seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","n":3}));seed(&mut e,"children",json!({"id":"c","parent":"p"}));adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();

#[test]
fn leaving_the_last_backfill_cannot_remove_an_ended_source_lifetime() {
 let old="table items:\n  n: int\n  until: time\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let next=old.replace("  until: time","  until: time\n  expire at .until")+"backfill items twice(n: int):\n  {n:n * 2}\n";
 for absent in [false,true] {
  let(s,p)=compile(old);let mut e=Engine::new_release_prepared_at(Store::memory().unwrap(),s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(1,None),false,0).unwrap();
  let r=wire::row_from_json(&e.schema().tables["items"],&json!({"id":"a","n":3,"until":50})).unwrap();e.seed_at([("items".into(),r)],0).unwrap();
  let(s,p)=compile(&next);e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(2,Some(1)),false,1).unwrap();
  if absent {let(s,p)=compile("query empty():\n  return true\n");e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(3,Some(2)),false,2).unwrap();}
  let previous=if absent {3}else{2};let(s,p)=compile(old);e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(1,Some(previous)),false,100).unwrap();assert_eq!(e.store().count("items").unwrap(),0);
 }
}

#[test]
fn saved_reference_inputs_keep_their_own_lifetime_after_live_retargeting() {
 for kind in ["parents","id"] {
 let parents="table parents:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let mutation="mutation retarget():\n  update children['c'] {parent:'q'}\n";
 let old=parents.to_owned()+"table children:\n  parent: parents on delete keep\n  public 'fixture'\n  update <- allow\n  online only\n"+mutation;
 let fill=format!("backfill children copy(parent: {kind}):\n  {{copied:(parents[parent] ! else NOT_FOUND).n}}\n");
 let next=old.replace("  parent: parents","  copied: int\n  parent: parents")+&fill;
 let dropped=next.replace("  parent: parents on delete keep\n","").replace(mutation,"");
 let mut e=engine(&old);for(id,n)in[("p",3),("q",9)]{seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":id,"n":n}));}seed(&mut e,"children",json!({"id":"c","parent":"p"}));adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();write(&mut e,"retarget");adopt(&mut e,&dropped,3).unwrap();
 let table=e.schema().tables["parents"].clone();{let tx=e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();let r=tx.get("parents","p").unwrap().unwrap();tx.delete("parents",&table,&r).unwrap();tx.commit().unwrap();}seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","n":77}));
 adopt(&mut e,parents,4).unwrap();let error=adopt(&mut e,&dropped,3).unwrap_err().to_string();assert!(error.contains("parent lifetime"),"{error}");
}
}

 let table=e.schema().tables["parents"].clone();{let tx=e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();let r=tx.get("parents","p").unwrap().unwrap();tx.delete("parents",&table,&r).unwrap();tx.commit().unwrap();}seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","name":"p"}));

}

#[test]
fn backfill_source_expiry_applies_cascade_set_null_and_restrict_atomically() {
 for action in ["cascade","set null","restrict"] {for restored in [false,true] {
  let optional=if action=="set null" {" ?"}else{""};
  let old=format!("table parents:\n  until: time\n  expire at .until\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\ntable children:\n  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}\n  cap 4 by parent\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\ntable items:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n");
  let next=old.replace("table items:\n  n:","table items:\n  doubled: int\n  n:")+"backfill items twice(n: int):\n  {doubled:n * 2}\n";
  let(s,p)=compile(&old);let mut e=Engine::new_release_prepared_at(Store::memory().unwrap(),s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(1,None),false,0).unwrap();
  let rows=[("parents",json!({"id":"p","until":50})),("children",json!({"id":"c","parent":"p"})),("items",json!({"id":"i","n":3}))];
  let rows=rows.into_iter().map(|(t,r)|(t.to_owned(),wire::row_from_json(&e.schema().tables[t],&r).unwrap())).collect::<Vec<_>>();e.seed_at(rows,0).unwrap();
  if restored {let(s,p)=compile("table items:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n");e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(2,Some(1)),false,1).unwrap();}
  let g=e.generation();let(s,p)=compile(&next);let result=e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(3,Some(if restored {2}else{1})),false,100);
  if action=="restrict" {let error=result.unwrap_err().to_string();assert!(error.contains("source expiry")&&error.contains("restrict"),"{error}");assert_eq!(g,e.generation());assert!(row(&mut e,"items","i").field("doubled").is_err());}
  else {result.unwrap();assert_eq!(e.store().count("parents").unwrap(),0);if action=="cascade" {assert_eq!(e.store().count("children").unwrap(),0);}else{assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"children","c","parent"),Value::Null);}assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","i","doubled"),Value::Int(6));}
 }}
}

  let next=old.replace("  n: int","  derived: int\n  n: int")+"backfill items twice(n: int):\n  {derived:n * 2}\n";

 }

fn source_expiry_observes_children_removed_in_the_same_release() {

  let optional=if action=="set null" {" ?"}else{""};

  let item="table items:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";

   if action=="cascade" {assert!(saved.is_none());}else{let saved:Value=serde_json::from_str(&saved.unwrap()).unwrap();assert_eq!(*saved.field("parent").unwrap(),Value::Null);}
  }

#[test]
fn physically_sparse_defaults_are_interpreted_and_receipts_keep_that_interpretation() {
 for kind in ["int","int ?"] {
  let old="table items:\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
  let defaulted=old.replace("  public","  n: int default 3\n  public");
  let fill=format!("backfill items twice(n: {kind}):\n  {{doubled:(n ?? 0) * 2}}\n");
  let next=defaulted.replace("  n:","  doubled: int\n  n:")+&fill;
  let mut e=engine(old);seed(&mut e,"items",json!({"id":"a"}));adopt(&mut e,&defaulted,2).unwrap();
  assert!(row(&mut e,"items","a").field("n").is_err(),"fixture is physically sparse");
  adopt(&mut e,&next,3).unwrap();assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","doubled"),Value::Int(6));
  let later=next.replace("default 3","default 100");adopt(&mut e,&later,4).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,"query empty():\n  return true\n",5).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&later,4).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","doubled"),Value::Int(6));
  let rollback=later.replace("  doubled: int\n","").replace(&fill,"");adopt(&mut e,&rollback,6).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&later,4).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","doubled"),Value::Int(6),"rollback/forward keeps the original omitted-input interpretation");
 }
}

//! Human preview groups facts about one affected table/operation once.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#15-wave-15-preview-and-rollback-day5 — full evidence remains available in JSON and verbose output.
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use snapback4_core::{Schema, ir::Program, store::DormantItem, successor::Step};
struct Group { warnings: Vec<String>, notes: Vec<String>, priority: u8 }
impl Default for Group { fn default() -> Self {Self {warnings:Vec::new(),notes:Vec::new(),priority:2}} }
fn table_prefix(text: &str, tables: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<String> {
    tables.iter().filter(|name|text.strip_prefix(name.as_str()).is_some_and(|tail|tail.is_empty() || tail.starts_with(['.',':',' ']))).max_by_key(|name|name.len()).cloned()
}
fn subject(text: &str, tables: &BTreeSet<String>, programs: &BTreeMap<String,Program>) -> String {
    // Read only generated subject positions, never arbitrary words inside an
    // authored predicate/refusal/value. Unknown formats remain release facts.
    if let Some(table)=table_prefix(text,tables) {return table;}
    for marker in ["table ","dependent ","backfill: "] {
        if let Some(tail)=text.strip_prefix(marker) && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    }
    let prefix=text.split(';').next().unwrap_or(text);
    if text.starts_with("queries/counts ") && let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" read ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    if text.starts_with("release ") && let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" safety dependencies on ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    if text.starts_with("rollback users get release ") {
        if let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" quotas on ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
        if let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once("'s ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    }
    if text.starts_with("release ") {
        if let Some(token)=prefix.split_whitespace().last() && let Some((owner,effect))=token.rsplit_once('.') {
            if effect=="require" {return format!("operation {owner}");}
            if tables.contains(owner) && matches!(effect,"read"|"insert"|"update"|"delete") {return owner.into();}
        }
        for name in programs.keys() {
            if prefix.ends_with(&format!(" operation {name}")) {return format!("operation {name}");}
        }
    }
    "release behavior".into()
}
fn brief(text: &str) -> String {
    // Semicolons also separate authored guards and multiple cap declarations;
    // retaining the full fact avoids dropping their contracts or caveats.
    text.to_owned()
}
pub(super) fn print(current: Option<&Schema>, target: &Schema, programs: &BTreeMap<String,Program>, warnings: &[String], notes: &[String], steps: &[Step], items: &[DormantItem]) {
    let tables: BTreeSet<_>=target.tables.keys().chain(current.into_iter().flat_map(|s|s.tables.keys())).cloned().collect();
    let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,Group>::new();
    for (warning, lines) in [(true,warnings),(false,notes)] {
        for line in lines {
            let group=groups.entry(subject(line,&tables,programs)).or_default();
            let priority=if line.contains("safety guard") || line.contains(".require;") {0} else if line.contains("confidentiality") || line.contains("safety rule") {1} else {2};
            group.priority=group.priority.min(priority);
            let text=if priority==0 {line.clone()} else {brief(line)};
            let dest=if warning {&mut group.warnings} else {&mut group.notes};
            if !dest.contains(&text) {dest.push(text);}
        }
    }
    for step in steps {
        let path=step.path.strip_prefix("tables.").unwrap_or(&step.path);
        let key=table_prefix(path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||path.to_owned());
        if path.strip_prefix(&key).is_some_and(|tail|tail.starts_with(".indexes.")) {continue;}
        let group=groups.entry(key).or_default();
        // Keep each user-visible source change even when another fact already
        // names this table. Only index plumbing is verbose-only.
        let detail=brief(&format!("{}: {}",path.replace(".columns.","."),step.message));
        if !group.notes.contains(&detail) {group.notes.push(detail);}
    }
    let mut storage=BTreeMap::<String,[u64;3]>::new();
    for item in items.iter().filter(|item|item.rows>0 && item.kind!="backfill") {
        let name=table_prefix(&item.path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||item.path.clone());
        let slot=match item.kind.as_str() {"column"=>1,"index"=>2,_=>0};
        storage.entry(name).or_default()[slot]+=item.rows;
    }
    for (name,[rows,cells,indexes]) in storage {
        groups.entry(name).or_default().notes.push(format!("retained: {rows} dormant rows, {cells} cells, {indexes} index entries"));
    }
    for item in items.iter().filter(|item|item.kind=="backfill" && item.rows>0) {
        let name=table_prefix(&item.path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||item.path.clone());
        groups.entry(name).or_default().notes.push(format!("retained: {} private backfill preimages ({} bytes)",item.rows,item.bytes));
    }
    let mut groups=groups.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    groups.sort_by_key(|(name,g)|(g.priority,name.clone()));
    for (name,mut group) in groups {
        let warning=!group.warnings.is_empty();
        group.warnings.append(&mut group.notes);
        println!("  {} {name}: {}{}",if warning {"WARNING"} else {"note:"},group.warnings.join("; "),if warning {"; verify these cases or preserve the current behavior in a bridge release"} else {""});
    }
}

//! Bind historical arguments without requiring them in the current row type.
use super::*;
use crate::{ast, diag::{type_error, unknown}, types::{Ty, scalar_to_column}};
use snapback4_core::schema::backfill::Backfill;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
pub(super) fn bind(catalog: &Catalog, schema: &mut Schema, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
    let mut names = BTreeSet::new(); let mut outputs = BTreeSet::new();
    for d in catalog.documents.iter().flat_map(|d| &d.backfills) {
        if !names.insert((d.table.clone(),d.name.clone())) { diagnostics.push(unknown(&d.site,"duplicate backfill name on this table","give each historical transform its own name")); continue; }
        let decl = ast::ProgramDecl { delivery: None, held:false, predicts:false, server:false, kind:ast::ProgramKind::Query,
            name: format!("backfill{}{}",d.table,d.name), args:d.args.clone(), prelude:vec![],
            body:vec![ast::Stmt::Return { value:d.value.clone(), site:d.site.clone() }], native:false, site:d.site.clone() };
        let Some(bound) = program::Binder::bind(catalog,schema,"schema",&decl,diagnostics) else {continue};
        let Ty::Object(fields) = &bound.result else { diagnostics.push(type_error(&d.site,"backfill returns an object patch","{ column: historicalValue }")); continue; };
        let Some(table) = schema.table(&d.table) else {diagnostics.push(unknown(&d.site,"backfill table is not declared","declare the candidate table"));continue};
        for (c,ty) in fields {
            if let Some(kind) = table.columns.get(c) {
                if !ty.assignable_to(&Ty::from_column(kind)) { diagnostics.push(type_error(&d.site,format!("backfill {}.{c} returns {}, expected {}",d.table,ty.name(),kind),"return a value fitting the candidate column")); }
            }
            if !outputs.insert((d.table.clone(),c.clone())) { diagnostics.push(type_error(&d.site,format!("backfills overlap on {}.{c}",d.table),"combine simultaneous outputs in one backfill")); }
        }
        let fill = Backfill { table:d.table.clone(), name:d.name.clone(), inputs:d.args.iter().map(|a|(a.name.clone(),scalar_to_column(&a.type_))).collect::<BTreeMap<_,_>>(), outputs:fields.keys().cloned().collect(), program:bound.program };
        if let Err(why) = fill.admit(schema) { diagnostics.push(type_error(&d.site,why,"use deterministic historical fields and a scalar patch").guide("deploy")); }
        schema.backfills.push(fill.normalized());
    }
}
//! A development reset: the adopted schema over an empty store, under a new
//! store identity, optionally reseeded, in one SQLite transaction.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.25 — what "fresh" keeps and what it empties; why the head keeps counting.
use super::*;

/// Tables a reset keeps whole: the store's own metadata, the catalog that
/// numbers tables and indexes, and the adopted generations.
const KEPT: [&str; 3] = ["_meta", "_catalog", "_generations"];

/// Identity tables a reset empties except for service seats: the dev
/// worker's session and `snapback4 token` seats outlive a reset, accounts,
/// guests and their sessions do not.
const SERVICE_SEATS: [(&str, &str); 5] = [
    ("_principals", "id"), ("_sessions", "principal"), ("_read_sessions", "principal"),
    ("_principal_generations", "principal"), ("_session_mint_bindings", "principal"),
];

/// What a development reset did. The caller unlinks `assets` after the
/// commit, outside any engine guard it holds.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DevReset {
    pub previous_store_id: String,
    pub store_id: String,
    /// The store's head after the reset and any reseed.
    pub seq: u64,
    pub seeded: u64,
    pub assets: assets::AssetSweep,
}

impl Engine {
    /// Empty every application table and everything derived from them
    /// (views, maintained columns, indexes, counts, the partition log),
    /// every queue (effects, jobs, actions), uploaded assets and every
    /// non-service account and session; keep the adopted schema and
    /// generation. The store takes a new identity so a connected device
    /// re-acquires instead of keeping its partition; the head keeps counting
    /// (the reset is itself a commit). `rows` are then written as `/seed`
    /// writes them, in the same transaction. Development only: the release
    /// host never calls this.
    pub fn dev_reset_at(&mut self, rows: Vec<(String, Value)>, now: i64) -> Result<DevReset, RuntimeError> {
        // Like adoption: no ephemeral program runs across the identity change.
        drop(self.ephemeral.lock()?);
        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000.000#2-fixture-semantics — the new store identity must not inherit the retired store's future clock.
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'time_audience_clock'", [])?;
        let now = time_audience::pin_writer_time(&self.schema, &tx, now)?;
        let previous_store_id = tx.meta("store_id")?.unwrap_or_default();
        let head = tx.next_seq()?.saturating_sub(1);
        let assets: Vec<String> = tx.conn().prepare("SELECT id FROM _assets")?.query_map([], |row| row.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
        let tables: Vec<String> = tx.conn()
            .prepare("SELECT name FROM main.sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite\\_%' ESCAPE '\\'")?
            .query_map([], |row| row.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.5 — every table empties together: no referential action runs, and no reference is left naming a removed row.
        for table in &tables {
            if KEPT.contains(&table.as_str()) { continue; }
            let quoted = format!("\"{}\"", table.replace('"', "\"\""));
            match SERVICE_SEATS.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == table) {
                Some((_, column)) => tx.conn().execute(&format!("DELETE FROM {quoted} WHERE substr({column}, 1, ?2) <> ?1"),
                    rusqlite::params![crate::identity::SERVICE_PREFIX, crate::identity::SERVICE_PREFIX.len() as i64])?,
                None => tx.conn().execute(&format!("DELETE FROM {quoted}"), [])?,
            };
        }
        // Prime at the reset clock in this transaction: no old period fires,
        // and the next crossed boundary fires normally. Replay's count restarts.
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key LIKE 'schedule:%' OR key LIKE 'schedule-shape:%' OR key = 'dev:suppressed-effects'", [])?;
        for schedule in &self.schema.schedules {
            tx.set_meta(&format!("schedule:{}", schedule.name), &schedule.boundary(now).to_string())?;
            tx.set_meta(&format!("schedule-shape:{}", schedule.name), &crate::value::digest(schedule))?;
        }
        tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _meta SET value = lower(hex(randomblob(16))) WHERE key = 'store_id'", [])?;
        let store_id = tx.meta("store_id")?.unwrap_or_default();
        // Every table changed: no change evidence may certify an interval
        // across the reset.
        tx.changes.borrow_mut().widen();
        let touched: Vec<String> = self.schema.visible_tables().map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).collect();
        tx.record_commit(head + 1, now, "dev reset", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, "reset", &touched, 0)?;
        if crate::store::backfills::has_evidence(&tx)? {crate::store::backfills::prepare_inputs(&tx,&self.schema,None)?;}
        let seeded = seed_rows(&self.schema, &tx, rows, now)?;
        let seq = tx.next_seq()?.saturating_sub(1);
        tx.commit()?;
        // A new store identity starts a fresh bounded expiry walk. Clear only
        // after commit so a refused reset keeps the old store's continuation.
        self.expiry_after.clear();
        self.timeline_schedule = timeline::Schedule::default();
        self.ephemeral.rebind_committed(store_id.clone(), self.generation, &self.schema);
        Ok(DevReset { previous_store_id, store_id, seq, seeded, assets: assets::AssetSweep::named(assets, self.store.assets_dir()) })
    }
}

    pub(super) fn delete(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
            ));
        }
        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| runner.delete_attempt(table_name, id))
    }

    fn delete_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
        self.refuse_receipt_scope_delete(table_name)?;
        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
        self.reserve_write_rules(table, &[Effect::Read, Effect::Delete])?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — delete prepays hidden contribution work before fetching its old image, with the same attempt lifetime as update.
        self.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
        })? else {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Require { site: Some(self.statement_site.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".to_owned(), message: None });
        };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — a delete that consults referencing rows needs read authority on its row first.
        let readable =
            !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)? && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
        if (self.schema.children(table_name).next().is_some() || self.schema.is_referenced(table_name)) && !readable
        {
            self.refusing_clause(table_name, "read rule");
            return Err(self.no_write_target());
        }
        if !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Delete, None, &old)? {
            return Err(if readable {
                RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.to_owned(), effect: Effect::Delete }
            } else { self.no_write_target() });
        }
        self.delete_authorized(table_name, old)
    }

    pub(super) fn delete_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let old = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, &old)?;
            // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — the actions may have changed the root (a maintained column mirrored from its children): remove its current image.
            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, &id))?.unwrap_or(old)
        } else { old };
        self.delete_row(table_name, old)
    }

    /// A delete's own removal of one row, its rules already decided: receipt
    /// membership, the read-through child probe, constraints, maintains and
    /// the partition event. A referential cascade removes each row this way.
    pub(super) fn delete_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
        self.receipt_member_removed(table_name, &old)?;
        self.refuse_live_children(table_name,old.field("id")?)?;
        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &old, Effect::Delete)?;
        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, &old)
        })?;
        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), None, entries)?;
        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), None, Origin::Source)
    }

    /// Remove a row the engine itself retires (an expired one): no rule and
    /// no constraint stands between the engine and its own sweep, while
    /// aggregates and partition events apply as for any delete.
    pub(super) fn remove(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, old)
        })?;
        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(old), None, entries)?;
        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(old), None, Origin::Source)
    }

    /// Physically retire one row whose upper lifetime ended. Expiry bypasses
    /// the root's authored delete rule and constraints, but it does not bypass
    /// the schema's declared effects on rows that reference the root. A
    /// read-through child still retains the expired parent physically.
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — expiry cleanup runs the same closure/restrict/set-null actions as an authored delete.
    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if self.physical_children(table_name, old.field("id")?)? { return Ok(false); }
        let current = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, old)?;
            // A cascade may maintain a column on the root; delete its current
            // physical image so index and cap entries match what is stored.
            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?;
            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))?
                .unwrap_or_else(|| old.clone())
        } else {
            old.clone()
        };
        self.remove(table_name, &current)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// At a program commit's end, retire every source row the commit changed
    /// or inserted whose lifetime has already ended: its final
    /// image was never live at a commit boundary, so it leaves no row for a
    /// later sweep to announce. Inside the commit the
    /// row existed as written (an insert-then-update still works). Engine
    /// bookkeeping, unmetered: the program's metering is already recorded.
    /// Server execution and device prediction both run it so a predicted
    /// final image cannot omit cascade, set-null or restrict effects. Its work,
    /// returned, stays
    /// linear in the rows retired: each aggregate row takes one net change
    /// and each audience key is scanned for a live row once. Seeds and loads
    /// ordinarily keep their rows for the sweep; row-keyed view sources use
    /// `retire_seeded_view_sources` to preserve their count-basis contract.
    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — a row whose lifetime ended by its own commit's end never exists at a commit boundary.
    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_births(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
        let Some(now) = self.context.now else { return Ok(Default::default());
        };
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#3 — an expired final image never grants a new recipient the row's id.
        // The tracker covers synced and unsynced source tables alike. Each
        // distinct entry prepaid its tree node, strings and this vector slot;
        // the rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
        // A row that existed before the commit and ends it already expired is
        // retired too: accounted from the partitions it was in at the commit's
        // start, it revokes there and announces nothing to a partition it only
        // entered with its expiring image.
        let mut changed: Vec<(String, String)> = std::mem::take(&mut self.expiry_rows).into_iter().collect();
        if changed.is_empty() {
            return Ok(Default::default());
        }
        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
        let order = self.schema.through_order();
        changed.sort_by_key(|(name,id)| {
            (std::cmp::Reverse(order.iter().position(|n| n == name)),id.clone(),
            )
        });
        // Server execution already reserved this bookkeeping in the source
        // writes. Device prediction instead runs the walk inside its separate
        // bounded physical-work meter: exhausting that allowance queues the
        // intent, never publishes a partial closure or refuses the write.
        let meter = if self.device_work_active { None } else {
            Some(std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort)))
        };
        self.retiring = Some(Default::default());
        let retired = changed.iter().try_for_each(|(table_name, id)| {
            let Some(row) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))? else { return Ok(());
            };
            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
            if table.expired(&row, now) { self.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row).map(|_| ()) } else { Ok(()) }
        });
        let aggregates = self.retiring.take().map(|retiring| retiring.aggregates).unwrap_or_default();
        let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));
        let work = meter.map(|meter| std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used).unwrap_or_default();
        retired.map(|()| work)
    }

    /// Seed writes historically retire only already-expired sources of
    /// row-keyed views. Keep that narrow boundary while routing their removal
    /// through the common action and net-maintenance path.
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.5 — ordinary expired fixtures remain stored; derived row-view sources cannot revive after clock rollback.
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub(crate) fn retire_seeded_view_sources(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        self.expiry_rows.retain(|(table, _)| schema.maintains.iter()
            .any(|maintain| maintain.source == table.as_str() && maintain.row_key.is_some()));
        self.retire_expired_births()
    }

    /// A column with a declared default takes it when the written row leaves
    /// it out, before validation and before the asset facts, so the row the
    /// rules and the constraints see is the complete one.
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — omitted defaults use the clock and viewer of the host running the insert.
    pub(super) fn with_defaults(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<Supplied, RuntimeError> {
        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
        if !table.defaults.keys().any(|name| {
            row.as_object().is_ok_and(|fields| !fields.contains_key(name))
        }) {
            return Ok(row);
        }
        let row = row.defaults(table,self.context.now.ok_or_else(||RuntimeError::Input("write clock is not pinned".into()))?,&self.context.viewer)?;
        self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?;
        Ok(row)
    }

    /// An `image`/`video` column names an upload by id; the row carries the
    /// facts the server established about it (type, bytes, dimensions,
    /// duration), never the client's word for them. The upload must be the
    /// writer's own and of the column's kind and size. The system principal
    /// may name an asset that was never uploaded: a fixture's placeholder,
    /// metadata only, never served.
    // Web stores hold received asset facts, never the authoritative upload ledger.
    #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
    fn with_asset_facts(&mut self, _table_name: &str, row: Value, _old: Option<&Value>, _hidden_patch: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(row)
    }

    pub(super) fn refuse_upsert_owned(&self, table: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Insert)?;
        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Update)
    }

    /// Programs never write a maintained target; the engine does.
    pub(super) fn refuse_engine_owned(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — pending member changes cannot rewrite settled requirements.
        if self.device && effect != Effect::Insert && self.schema.receipts.iter().any(|f| f.members == table || f.runs == table) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt membership changes and progress queue until settlement".into()));
        }
        self.refuse_receipt_table(table)?;
        self.refuse_condition_write()?;
        self.refuse_timeline_write(table, effect)?;
        self.schema.refuse_private(table)?;
        if self.schema.maintain_for(table).is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table} is a maintained aggregate; write its source rows instead")));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

//! Ownership locks the database's sidecar; stat pins its inode. `serve.lock` is only an address hint.
use std::{fs::{self, File}, io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write}, path::{Path, PathBuf}, time::Duration};
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError, Store};
#[cfg(unix)]
use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;

pub(crate) struct Owner {
    _sidecar: std::sync::Arc<File>,
    identity: (u64, u64),
    path: PathBuf,
    record: Option<File>,
    reclaimed: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) token_authority: Option<crate::serve::token::Authority>,
}

/// The address `doctor` dials for the server that owns this store: the
/// published loopback address itself, or, for a wildcard bind, that family's
/// loopback on the same port. A published non-loopback address is not followed.
pub(crate) fn inspector_address(store: &Path) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    let path = store.canonicalize().ok()?;
    dialable(&address(&path)?)
}

fn dialable(published: &str) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr, SocketAddr};
    let address = published.strip_prefix("http://")?.parse::<SocketAddr>().ok()?;
    let ip = match address.ip() {
        ip if ip.is_loopback() => ip,
        IpAddr::V4(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST),
        IpAddr::V6(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST),
        _ => return None,
    };
    (address.port() != 0).then(|| SocketAddr::new(ip, address.port()))
}

fn resolve(store: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    match store.canonicalize() {
        Ok(path) => Ok(path),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
            let parent = store.parent().filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty()).unwrap_or(Path::new("."));
            snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(parent).map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?;
            Ok(parent.canonicalize().map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?.join(store.file_name().ok_or("store path has no filename")?))
        }
        Err(e) => Err(failure(store, e)),
    }
}

fn failure(path: &Path, reason: impl std::fmt::Display) -> String {
    format!("E_STORE at {}: {reason}; restore a regular store/address file and retry", path.display())
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn same_file(a: &fs::Metadata, b: &fs::Metadata) -> bool { a.dev() == b.dev() && a.ino() == b.ino() }

#[cfg(unix)]
fn regular(path: &Path, create: bool, database: &Path) -> Result<File, String> {
    snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(database, path, create, 128)
        .map_err(|e| failure(path, e))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — sidecar flocks fence backend writers and share device ownership without locking SQLite.
pub(crate) fn command(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, false, Duration::ZERO) }
pub(crate) fn device(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, true, Duration::ZERO) }
// @ref LLP 3000.009#5.3 — a restarting host waits for watchdogs to finish group cleanup.
pub(crate) fn host(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, false, Duration::from_secs(5)) }

#[cfg(unix)]
fn acquire(store: &Path, shared: bool, wait: Duration) -> Result<Owner, String> {
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + wait;
    for _ in 0..16 {
        let path = resolve(store)?;
        snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(path.parent().ok_or("store path has no parent")?)
            .map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        // Stat before opening either auxiliary file; a refused probe creates
        // no database. Only the sidecar lock grants permission to create one.
        let before = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        let sidecar = snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_file(&path)
            .map_err(|e| failure(&snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&path), e))?;
        let mut cleanup = None;
        loop {
            let locked = if shared { sidecar.try_lock_shared() } else { sidecar.try_lock() };
            match locked {
                Ok(()) => break,
                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) if std::time::Instant::now() < deadline && *cleanup.get_or_insert_with(|| stopped_host(&path)) => std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)),
                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => return Err(busy(&path)),
                Err(fs::TryLockError::Error(error)) => return Err(failure(&path, error)),
            }
        }
        if !snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_is_named(&path, &sidecar) { continue; }
        snapback4_core::private_fs::database_file(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        let database = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?
            .ok_or_else(|| failure(&path, "database disappeared during ownership acquisition"))?;
        if before.as_ref().is_some_and(|old| !same_file(old, &database)) { continue; }
        let mut reclaimed = None;
        let record = if shared { None } else {
            let record_path = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
            if let Some(pid)=owner_pid(&path) {
                if unsafe {libc::kill(pid as libc::pid_t,0)} == -1 && std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error()==Some(libc::ESRCH) {
                    reclaimed = Some(format!("reclaimed stale serve.lock: dead PID {pid}; directory {}", path.parent().unwrap().display()));
                }
            }
            let file = regular(&record_path, true, &path)?;
            file.set_len(0).map_err(|e| failure(&record_path, e))?;
            Some(file)
        };
        return Ok(Owner { _sidecar: std::sync::Arc::new(sidecar), identity: (database.dev(), database.ino()), path, record, reclaimed, token_authority: None });
    }
    Err(failure(store, "database path kept changing during ownership acquisition"))
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn acquire(store: &Path, _: bool, _: Duration) -> Result<Owner, String> { Err(failure(store, "database ownership requires Unix")) }

pub(crate) fn stopped_host(path: &Path) -> bool {
    // A CLI owner or a host not yet announced still refuses immediately. A
    // reachable listener does too; only a prior host's cleanup gets a wait.
    // This is a refusal/wait hint, never permission to open the store: the
    // sidecar must still be acquired. Never dial a non-loopback address hint.
    address(path).is_some_and(|published| dialable(&published).is_none_or(|address|
        std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, Duration::from_millis(50)).is_err()))
}

pub(crate) fn busy(path: &Path) -> String {
    let owner = address(path).map(|address| match owner_pid(path) { Some(pid) => format!("{address} (pid {pid})"), None => address })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "another CLI command or a server starting up (address pending)".into());
    format!("E_STORE_BUSY at {}: this store is live; owned by {owner}; directory {}; no work was admitted. Stop its `snapback4 dev` or `snapback4 serve` process (or wait for the owning CLI command), rerun this command once, then restart the server. Exclusion holds while <database>-owner is left in place; deleting or replacing it while a process runs ends exclusion and does not stop that process", path.display(),path.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(".")).display())
}

#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) fn address(path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    // A missing/replaced address record cannot grant ownership. Never follow
    // a symlink (including one to the database), nor block on a FIFO.
    let record = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
    let file = regular(&record, false, path).ok()?;
    let mut text = String::new();
    file.take(1024).read_to_string(&mut text).ok()?;
    let mut lines = text.lines();
    let port = lines.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u16>().ok());
    lines.next().map(str::to_owned).or_else(|| port.map(|p| format!("http://127.0.0.1:{p}")))
}

/// The owning host's PID from its address record (`pid N` on the third line).
#[cfg(unix)]
fn owner_pid(path: &Path) -> Option<u32> {
    let record = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
    let file = regular(&record, false, path).ok()?;
    let mut text = String::new();
    file.take(1024).read_to_string(&mut text).ok()?;
    text.lines().nth(2)?.strip_prefix("pid ")?.parse().ok()
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn owner_pid(_: &Path) -> Option<u32> { None }

#[cfg(not(unix))]
pub(crate) fn address(_: &Path) -> Option<String> { None }

impl Owner {
    pub(crate) fn report_reclaim(&self, verbose: bool) {
        if verbose && let Some(note) = &self.reclaimed { eprintln!("note: {note}"); }
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#11-wave-11-factual-release-narration — unlink only our address inode; the ownership sidecar remains named.
    pub(crate) fn clear_address(&self) {
        #[cfg(unix)]
        if let Some(file) = &self.record {
            let path = self.path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
            if let (Ok(held), Ok(named)) = (file.metadata(), fs::symlink_metadata(&path))
                && same_file(&held, &named) {
                let _ = fs::remove_file(path);
            }
        }
    }
    pub(crate) fn worker_lock(&self) -> std::sync::Arc<File> { self._sidecar.clone() }

    pub(crate) fn path(&self) -> Result<&Path, RuntimeError> {
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let meta = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&self.path)
                .map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(failure(&self.path, e)))?;
            if meta.is_some_and(|m| (m.dev(), m.ino()) == self.identity) { return Ok(&self.path); }
        }
        Err(RuntimeError::Store(failure(&self.path, "owned database moved or was replaced; stop and reopen its current path")))
    }

    pub(crate) fn open_store(&self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Store, RuntimeError> {
        let mut store = Store::open_with_busy_timeout(self.path()?, timeout)?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        store.retain_ownership(self._sidecar.clone())?;
        Ok(store)
    }

    pub(crate) fn open_engine(&self, bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound, timeout: Duration, now: i64) -> Result<Engine, RuntimeError> {
        let store = self.open_store(timeout)?;
        if store.meta("release")?.is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("this store belongs to a deployment; use `deploy` to activate source and `serve` to run it".into()));
        }
        Engine::new_at(store, bound.schema.clone(), bound.programs.iter().map(|p| p.program.clone()), now)
    }
}

impl Drop for Owner { fn drop(&mut self) { self.clear_address(); } }

pub(crate) fn announce(owner: &mut Owner, address: std::net::SocketAddr) -> Result<(), String> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — live token work runs through the owner, with proof of local store access.
    owner.token_authority = Some(crate::serve::token::publish(owner.path().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)
        .map_err(|e| failure(&owner.path, e))?);
    let file = owner.record.as_mut().ok_or("device ownership has no server address record")?;
    file.set_len(0).and_then(|_| file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    // First-line port is retained for the dev inspector; the third line names the owning process.
    write!(file, "{}\nhttp://{address}\npid {}\n", address.port(), std::process::id()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}
